newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil orders Brahma-Miller to undo joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Brazil orders Brahma-Miller to undo joint venture.

text.p: A Brazilian anti-trust body has ordered brewers Brahma and Miller Brewing Co to dissolve their joint venture within 24 months because it was found to impede competition, an official said.
The seven members of the government's Administrative Economic Defence Council (Cade) ruled 5-2 against the Brahma-Miller joint venture set up in 1995, the official said.

Under the venture, which had been due to expire in 2010, Brahma sold and distributed Miller products in Brazil, giving its parent company Philip Morris Cos Inc a foothold in the booming Brazilian beer market.
The Cade official said the vote took place late Wednesday night and that no one was immediately available to comment on the reasons behind the ruling.

Newspaper Gazeta Mercantil said the five members of the council who voted against the joint venture believed Miller could have entered the Brazilian market on its own, improving competition in the sector.

"The means chosen by Miller was the easiest, the cheapest," the newspaper quoted Renault de Freitas Castro, the Cade member who oversaw the case, as saying. "But that was not the only way in and it does not satisfy the interests of competition."
He said Miller would be able to set up its own breweries in Brazil and draw up a new strategy within two years.
Among the two members who voted in favor of the venture was Cade president Gesner de Oliveira. He told Gazeta Mercantil the decision represented excessive intervention in the market.
Brahma and Miller have 30 days to inform Cade if they accept with the ruling. They may also appeal the decision.
